mostWorthwhile.text: Observing Jupiter’s moons was most worthwhile: it challenges the idea that everything circles Earth directly while making clear that this alone does not prove Earth moves.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the telescope was necessary but less engaging as the only available opening action.

surprise.text: The Moon’s rough surface challenged the assumed contrast between perfect heavens and imperfect Earth.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; the offered combinations made each observation’s immediate goal clear.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the Venus observations distinguish competing models; the result established a constraint but left that comparison open.
